note: Independent rejudgment 2026-11-24 against RFC 7858 Section 3.1 (rfc/full/rfc7858.txt): "DNS clients MUST NOT send and DNS servers MUST NOT respond to cleartext DNS messages on any port used for DNS over TLS (including, for example, after a failed TLS handshake)." Verified changes since dcc219072a (cd9c79b63c): TestDoTListener (positive: TLS-wrapped query on DoT port answered with A record) and TestDoTRefusesCleartext (negative: raw TCP cleartext query failing TLS handshake receives no DNS answer) are unchanged. Two new tagged geodns config tests strengthen the "any port used for DNS over TLS" clause: TestGeoDNSListenerOnDoTListenPortRefused (negative) verifies parseListeners calls dnsserver.RefuseCleartextOnConfiguredDoTPort to refuse a cleartext listener sharing a custom DoT listen-port (8853) with the exact operator fix, and TestGeoDNSListenerOffDoTListenPortAccepted (positive) proves the refusal is gated on DoT being enabled on that port. Verified dnsresolver serves no DoT and as112 cleartext is fixed on port 53 (refused as DoT port). Verdict stands: enforced.
